newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call steady, gilts quiet ahead of auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian call steady, gilts quiet ahead of auction.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday at 0.1-0.4 percent, little changed from opening quotes of 0.1-0.25 percent, dealers said.

They said there was little trade during the day as there were few borrowers in a market flush with funds. "Call money will remain easy," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Even the outflows at the auctions later today should not have much impact."
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) holds a four-day repo auction of government securities and an auction of 30 billion rupees of 10-year bonds later on Monday.
Dealers said funds outflows towards the auctions could push call money rates up marginally.
"Call money may go up to 1.0 percent or slightly above," said a dealer. "But I do not see rates going up much beyond that."
Dealers said there was moderate trade in government securities as market players awaited the auction results.
They said they were looking to the auction results as a signal of the future direction of long-term interest rates.
"If the cut-off on the 10-year bond is above 13.10 percent, I think we may see a correction in security prices," said a dealer. "We may then see some fall in prices."
